name: Ice-shedding wing skin
subtitle: a wing skin that sheds ice without heaters

effects.effect: microscopic bumps make water bead up and roll off, carrying dirt away
capsules in a plastic burst when it cracks and glue the crack shut

effect: microscopic bumps make water bead up and roll off, carrying dirt away
how: Ice on wings and rotor blades still brings down aircraft, and today's fixes are heaters or chemical sprays that cost fuel and time. A skin covered in microscopic bumps makes supercooled droplets bounce off before they can freeze, and capsules under the surface burst to refill scratches so the texture survives rain and grit.
obstacle: Water-repelling textures wear away within hours under rain at flight speeds, faster than any self-repair so far.
why: Anti-icing textures pass wind-tunnel tests; none is certified on an aircraft.
real: Superhydrophobic and self-healing anti-icing coatings tested in icing tunnels and on UAV propellers; no self-healing textured skin on an aircraft.
